what_it_does: Data centers and modern processors need power converters that can deliver large amounts of current (12 amperes) at very low voltages (down to 1 volt), while doing so efficiently and keeping voltage stable even during sudden demand spikes. This converter uses a two-step approach: first, it steps down the input voltage (12V) to an intermediate level using a bulk converter that's very efficient, then a second stage uses switched-capacitor regulators (devices that switch capacitors in and out of the circuit to regulate voltage) fine-tuned for stable resonant operation. Together they achieve nearly 90% efficiency and keep voltage undershoot to just 26 millivolts—meaning the voltage barely sags when current demand suddenly jumps.
